short_desc: Species of birch native to eastern North America.
full_desc: Betula lenta (sweet birch, black birch, or cherry birch) is a species of birch native to eastern North America, from southern Maine west to southernmost Ontario, and south in the Appalachian Mountains to northern Georgia. The bark smells strongly of wintergreen when scraped and produces oil of wintergreen upon distillation.

short_desc: Herbaceous perennial flowering plant known for hollow stinging hairs.
full_desc: Urtica dioica, commonly known as stinging nettle, is a herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Urticaceae. Originally native to Europe, much of temperate Asia and western North Africa, it is now found worldwide. The leaves and stems possess hollow stinging hairs (trichomes) containing histamine and other chemicals that produce a stinging sensation upon contact.

short_desc: Flowering shrub in the legume family native to North America.
full_desc: Amorpha fruticosa is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by several common names, including desert false indigo, false indigo-bush, and bastard indigobush. It grows as a glandular, thornless deciduous shrub up to 5 meters tall. It has clusters of small purple to blue flowers with single petals and long stamens.

short_desc: Perennial flowering shrub cultivated for castor oil seeds.
full_desc: Ricinus communis, the castor bean or castor oil plant, is a species of perennial flowering plant in the spurge family, Euphorbiaceae. It is the sole species in the monotypic genus Ricinus. Its seed is the castor bean, which, despite its name, is not a true bean, and contains the toxin ricin as well as castor oil.

short_desc: Herbaceous perennial with tubular white flowers native to North America.
full_desc: Penstemon digitalis, known by the common name foxglove beardtongue or talus slope penstemon, is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family. Native to eastern and central North America, it produces upright stalks with opposite lanceolate leaves and showy tubular white to pink blossoms favored by native pollinators.

short_desc: Species of sunflower native to central North America with edible tubers.
full_desc: Helianthus tuberosus, also called sunroot, sunchoke, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America. It is cultivated widely across the temperate zone for its edible tuber, which is crisp, nutty, and rich in the prebiotic fiber inulin.

short_desc: Familiar flowering herbaceous perennial with bright yellow composite flowers.
full_desc: Taraxacum officinale, the common dandelion, is a flowering herbaceous perennial plant of the dandelion genus in the family Asteraceae. Celebrated for its bright yellow flower heads that turn into fluffy white seed clocks, it is fully edible, resilient, and widely distributed across temperate regions.

short_desc: Epiphytic vine with dramatic perforated fenestrated leaves.
full_desc: Monstera deliciosa, the Swiss cheese plant or split-leaf philodendron, is a species of flowering plant native to tropical forests of southern Mexico, south to Panama. It is widely grown in temperate zones as a houseplant for its dramatic fenestrated leaves.
